objective: Replace open-ended enumeration of native-extension and nonprocess parent effects with one kernel-enforced parent runtime membrane plus one complete broker authority.

assumptions: ENTRY_DOMINANCE: every credited production Brain capability execution that can produce terminally relevant external effects begins inside the bound parent namespace membrane before untrusted repo code, third-party Python, native extensions, or task code can run.

NO_AMBIENT_EFFECT_CHANNEL: the confined process has no host network namespace, no writable host filesystem mount, no host PID/IPC/UTS namespace, no Linux capabilities, no privilege escalation, no undeclared inherited file descriptor, and no externally material writable device or socket channel.

BROKER_TOTALITY: every externally material effect required by a credited capability is represented as a typed broker request over the sole inherited broker channel and is denied unless a content-addressed final authorizer accepts it.
BROKER_POSTCONDITIONS: committed broker effects are independently receipted and checked against class-specific authority, resource, safety, and provenance postconditions.
PERSISTENCE_TOTALITY: durable Brain state leaves the confined runtime only through an explicitly authorized persistence broker or a separately proved equivalent channel.
KERNEL_BOUNDARY_ASSUMPTION: the Linux namespace, mount, descriptor, privilege and resource controls behave according to the independently replayed substrate contract on the production carrier.
theorem.conclusion: For the bound execution universe, native-extension internal syscalls, direct socket attempts, direct filesystem mutation attempts, child-process attempts and other nonprocess implementation details cannot create a terminally relevant host external material effect outside the broker-authorized effect set. Therefore Root3 native/nonprocess effect-totality proof reduces from enumerating implementation APIs to proving ENTRY_DOMINANCE + BROKER_TOTALITY + BROKER_POSTCONDITIONS + PERSISTENCE_TOTALITY for the production carrier.
proof_sketch: A native or interpreted operation can affect terminal truth externally only through some kernel-visible carrier such as network, filesystem/device, process/IPC namespace, inherited descriptor, privilege, or broker.
The membrane removes or privatizes every listed ambient carrier and drops privilege needed to reacquire host-level authority.
Undeclared inherited descriptors are absent, leaving the declared broker as the only intentional cross-boundary capability channel.
Therefore any credited external material effect must either traverse the broker or violate a membrane premise.
Broker totality and postcondition checks then reduce effect authorization to the typed, content-addressed authority relation rather than implementation language or library identity.
